claims.text: The single ERP line on the receipt — SGD 3.20 for the 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' gantry at (1.34, 103.78) — is a phantom charge. The platform's own proximity computation against the trace places the vehicle's closest fix 7,482.07 m from that gantry, roughly thirty times the 250 m radius POL-RD-09 uses to treat a fix as a crossing. On the only measurement in the record the car never came near the gantry, let alone passed it.

The ledger condemns itself. The fare_breakdown itemises the very same gantry with on_optimal_route set to false, and the trip_record's routing snapshot bills SGD 0.00 of optimal-route ERP. The billing system's own field says the gantry is not on the route the platform sold; the only live question is why the rider was charged for it anyway.

A charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes is, by the express words of POL-RD-09(4), a billing-integrity failure refunded in full as a standalone correction, and that limb is available whether or not any deviation exists. The full SGD 3.20 must be returned and the matter recorded as a billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4). This does not engage POL-RD-10(8): that sub-clause carves out precisely the case where the only unmatched line is one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), so there is no basis to withhold the money and escalate instead.

Independently of the phantom-gantry analysis, POL-RD-11(a) gives the rider any amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote plus properly chargeable pass-through lines. This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: quoted_fare_sgd is 22.00 and charged_total is 25.20. The pass-through deductible is nil — no ERP was actually crossed, there are no tolls, the trip does not originate at an airport so no surcharge is chargeable, and waiting_time_fee is 0.00. The whole 3.20 excess is therefore refunded in full.

The contested amount is SGD 3.20 and the refund is SGD 3.20. The filing party is entirely right and the whole contested amount is returned, which is the definition of FULL_REFUND under POL-GEN-03. Even read as a pass-through correction, the rider recovers the entire disputed line rather than a fraction of it.

The driver does not contradict the rider on the decisive fact. His statement on file records that he 'did not see or pass the gantry named on the receipt'. The only party who could speak to the crossing concedes the point, and the trace measurement agrees with him.

For completeness, the trip's own trace establishes a route deviation: excess is 3.5 km, or 28.00% of the 12.5 km optimal, clearing both POL-RD-01 gates (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%). It is not a MATERIAL deviation (below 50% and below 8.0 km), so no POL-RD-06 uplift arises, and because the fare model is UPFRONT_QUOTE, POL-RD-11 bars any distance-or-time refund. The rider's recovery is confined to the phantom pass-through line, and that is all this brief claims.

No traffic advisory exists for this trip. EV-ADVIS-09114-01 is MISSING — issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0 — so there is no artifact naming a road the optimal route traverses with a validity window overlapping the trip. POL-RD-03 exoneration is unavailable to the driver on this record, and his burden under POL-RD-08(b) is undischarged: the off-route driving stands unexplained, not excused.

The identity condition in POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-09114 with the same pickup event at 11:30 on 2026-09-21, and the excess clears the POL-RD-01 threshold. The rider's initial burden is therefore discharged and the burden shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause — a burden the missing advisory leaves him unable to meet.

No corroboration overlay applies. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the four-or-more condition in POL-RD-08 is not met and no evidence beyond the trace is required. The rider relies on no other profile field; prior_no_show_flags and prior_deviation_flags are context only under POL-GEN-01 and carry no weight for either side here.

The deviation therefore carries no money on the distance and time lines and cannot be used to inflate the contested amount beyond the disputed pass-through line.

Measured on the governing trace figure the excess is 3.5 km and 28.0% - trace_distance_km 16.0 km on EV-GPS-09114 against the booked optimal 12.5 km on EV-TRIP-09114 - which satisfies POL-RD-01 but does not reach MATERIAL, being below both the 50% and the 8.0 km thresholds. The POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is therefore not triggered and no FULL_REFUND uplift of charged_total is available.

Even if POL-RD-06 were consulted, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 610 (EV-DPROF-09114), far below the three-flag and 5% tests, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and neither the rider-favourable balancing in limb (a) nor the conduct referral in limb (c) can follow. No DRIVER_COMPENSATION is available on this record: the rider was billed for exactly the 16.0 km the trace records - distance_charged_km 16.0 on EV-FARE-09114 against trace_distance_km 16.0 on EV-GPS-09114 - so the POL-RD-04 unbilled-distance shortfall is zero and the 0.75 per km limb cannot run; the chat_log carries a single message (waypoint_hint null) with no rider instruction to detour, so the detour-exoneration limb cannot run either.

That 3.20 is the ceiling of the rider's recovery; no other line is contested and no other line is off-route.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes - COMPLETE, 100% coverage, no gap above 30 seconds (max_gap_sec 0.0) on EV-GPS-09114 - so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) does not operate and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; the only charge line with no counterpart in the trace is the ERP line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly carves out. The record is complete and consistent (trip id TRP-09114 across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; pickup 11:30 agreeing with the first fix), so this is a simple pass-through correction and the disputed 3.20 need not be held pending review.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver — here is the decision and the reasoning behind it.

THE FACTS ARE AGREED. This was an upfront-quoted trip (quoted_fare_sgd SGD 22.00). The receipt adds one ERP charge of SGD 3.20 for the 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' gantry, bringing the total charged to SGD 25.20. On the trace the car's closest fix to that gantry is 7,482 m away — about thirty times the 250 m radius this policy uses to treat a fix as a crossing — the fare ledger's own field marks that gantry on_optimal_route = false, the trip record bills SGD 0.00 of optimal-route ERP, and the driver's own on-file statement records that he did not pass the gantry named. The car never crossed the gantry. The SGD 3.20 line is a phantom charge — a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4).

THE OUTCOME. The SGD 3.20 is refunded in full. Because the whole of the contested amount is returned to the rider, the ruling is FULL_REFUND. The refund is rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 and stays at SGD 3.20.

WHY ONLY THE ERP LINE MOVES. This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip, so POL-RD-11 governs and the distance and time charges were fixed at booking. POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront trip: however long the routing, the rider loses nothing on distance or time, and no distance-or-time refund is available. The rider's recovery on money is limited to (a) the amount by which the total charged exceeds the quote plus pass-throughs properly chargeable under POL-RD-09, and (b) the pass-through correction for a phantom gantry. The pass-through deductible here is nil — no ERP was actually crossed, there are no tolls, the trip does not originate at an airport so no surcharge is chargeable, and the waiting fee is 0.00 — so the whole SGD 3.20 by which charged_total (25.20) exceeds the quote (22.00) is refunded in full. Both sides' figures agree on this ceiling.

THE DEVIATION. The trace does establish a route deviation: 16.0 km against the 12.5 km booked optimal, an excess of 3.5 km and 28.0%, clearing both POL-RD-01 gates (over 0.8 km and over 20%). It is not a MATERIAL deviation (below 50% and below 8.0 km). On an upfront trip this changes no money, and the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check finds no repeat pattern — deviation_flags_90d 0 against 610 completed trips — so no driver-conduct referral arises either.

THE DRIVER'S EXONERATION ROUTES. The traffic-advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-09114-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) and carries no fact, so the POL-RD-03 closure route is unavailable; the chat log holds a single message with no rider instruction and waypoint_hint null, so the POL-RD-04 rider-requested detour route does not run; and the trip record shows no amended pickup or dropoff, so POL-RD-05 does not apply. None of this changes the money — the rider recovers the ERP line whether or not any deviation exists.

NO DRIVER COMPENSATION. The rider was billed for exactly the distance the trace records (16.0 km billed against 16.0 km on the trace), so the POL-RD-04 unbilled-distance shortfall is zero and the 0.75-per-km limb cannot run.

NO ESCALATION. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes — complete, 100% coverage, no gap over 30 seconds — so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged. The only charge line with no counterpart in the trace is the ERP line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly carves out. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires and the disputed amount is not held.

CONFIDENCE. 0.95. The deciding fact — that the gantry was never crossed — is carried by two artifacts at full weight: the GPS trace (EV-GPS-09114, nearest fix 7,482 m) and the fare ledger (EV-FARE-09114, on_optimal_route false). Under POL-GEN-02(2) the cap is the maximum of the independent carriers, i.e. 1.0; the bundle mean is context only and is not the cap. The driver's statement is further evidence but carries no weight_multiplier, so it enters neither the minimum nor the maximum of the cap.

No claim was discarded at the citation stage.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity — refund the phantom SGD 3.20 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' ERP line in full as a standalone pass-through correction and record the billing defect for review; the trace's nearest fix to the gantry is 7,482 m, far outside the 250 m crossing radius, and the fare ledger marks the gantry on_optimal_route = false.
